20261126-pleiotropy-promotes-divergence-.headline: Pleiotropy promotes divergence when simulating the development and evolution of two interacting organs
20261126-pleiotropy-promotes-divergence-.dek: Pleiotropy, which can occur when a gene affects multiple traits, is a central property of living organisms, influencing their response to mutations and their evolutionary trajectories.
20261126-pleiotropy-promotes-divergence-.summary: Despite many studies and discussions, it remains very difficult to reconcile molecular, developmental and quantitative evolutionary genetics viewpoints on pleiotropy and appreciate how much it puts constraints on genetic evolution, phenotypic evolution and adaptation. Here, we revisit this question by simulating evolution in silico. (bioRxiv)

20261126-exploring-roles-temperature-com.headline: Exploring the roles of temperature and competition in Fennoscandic Holocene plant communities using dynamic sedimentary ancient DNA models
20261126-exploring-roles-temperature-com.dek: Ecosystems are constantly responding to shifting environmental conditions, and the observed structure of ecological communities at any given discrete observation timepoint is part of a larger dynamic response.
20261126-exploring-roles-temperature-com.summary: However, we lack long-term time series of ecosystem responses allowing understanding of the processes driving community dynamics. Sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) offers novel opportunities to link empirical data with ecological processes, providing near continuous records of plant and animal community changes over millennia. (bioRxiv)
